title: Sidecarless span-attach hook for chunked/streaming responses
creator: Marcus Chen
description:
Problem: Long-lived or chunked responses (server-sent events, chunked HTTP, gRPC server streaming, WebSocket message streams) currently produce incomplete or misleading trace data. Parent spans often close on first response chunk or when request handler returns, missing tail latency and post-response errors (upload/flush failures, backend retries, finalization errors). This makes our latency/error dashboards under-count streaming tail latency and hides bursty error modes for customers using streaming APIs.

Goal: Implement a sidecarless, low-overhead SDK/middleware hook that can: 1) attach a lightweight span to an outgoing response stream, 2) defer span completion until an explicit end-of-stream or timeout, 3) propagate a deterministic request fingerprint across services and proxies, and 4) be toggled per-route via config. The hook should work across Node/Python/Go SDKs and interoperate with OTLP/trace-proxy and our existing trace headers.

Scope & non-goals: We are not introducing a network sidecar or changing transport protocols. This is SDK-level instrumentation and server-server header conventions only. We will not change the public API for customers; the feature is opt-in via environment flag or route config initially.

Acceptance criteria:
- Node SDK prototype attaches stream spans and preserves parent linkage for chunked responses.
- Per-request fingerprint header set for streaming routes: X-RW-STREAM-ID (32 hex chars) and sampling bit marker.
- End-to-end tests demonstrate tail latency captured for HTTP chunked, SSE, gRPC server streaming and WebSocket close.
- Overhead target: <1% CPU at 5k rps and <2% memory increase.
- Console dashboard updated to surface 'stream tail latency' percentile and error count for streaming routes.

Design summary:
- Hook model: add a ResponseStream.attachSpan(spanOptions) middleware that returns a handle. When the server writes the first chunk or when middleware is invoked, the SDK ensures a span is created and linked to the request's parent trace. The handle exposes done(error) to close the span. If done is not called, a safe timeout (configurable, default 30s) completes the span with a timeout status.
- Request fingerprint: deterministic 128-bit hex derived from request ID + route + sampling salt; encoded in X-RW-STREAM-ID and hashed for compactness. Header includes a low-overhead sampling bit to allow deterministic client-side sampling decisions without contacting control plane.
- Registry: SDK maintains an ephemeral WeakMap/weakref registry keyed by response stream object to avoid leaks. The registry stores only span reference and a 16-byte id.
- Propagation: header is passed downstream; if a proxy strips unknown headers, we fall back to query param token for internal traffic only (flagged).
- Telemetry export: emit an OTLP event type "stream.chunk" at first write and "stream.end" at completion with final status and bytes_sent. These events feed existing trace-indexed logs and our metrics pipeline to populate the new dashboard metrics.

Prototype results (Node):
- Microbenchmark: express/middleware prototype at 5k rps (POST streaming) shows +0.12% CPU and +0.6% memory.
- End-to-end: captured additional 95th percentile tail latency in streaming route (example service) from 120ms -> 480ms; uncovered a retry-on-close bug in backend used by a customer.

Open design decisions:
1) Header format vs dedicated cookie: header chosen for simplicity and cross-language parity; cookie would not work for websocket/gRPC.
2) Deterministic sampling placement: sampling bit added to X-RW-STREAM-ID vs separate header. Chosen to avoid header explosion.
3) Timeout semantics: default 30s but must be route-configurable. Edge case: connection that remains idle should not keep span open indefinitely; we use an idle timeout (configurable).

Implementation plan:
- Week 1: finalize API surface and add spec doc; Node prototype refinement. (Marcus)
- Week 2: add Python SDK equivalent and integration tests; update trace-proxy to forward X-RW-STREAM-ID. (Ava, Priya)
- Week 3: add Go SDK implementation and cross-language e2e suites; produce performance report. (Ava, Lin)
- Week 4: Console work to add 'stream tail latency' widget and error count; prepare rollout playbook. (Observability UX)
